chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, raising it from Abi Abdillah (عليه السلام), said:

While Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was delivering a sermon upon the pulpit of al-Kufah, a man known as Dhi'lib stood up before him, eloquent in speech and brave of heart. He said, "O Amir al-Mu'minin, have you seen your Lord?" He (عليه السلام) said, "Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! I would not worship a Lord whom I had not seen."

He said, "O Amir al-Mu'minin, how did you see Him?" He (عليه السلام) said, "Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! Eyes do not see Him through the sight of vision, but hearts see Him through the realities of iman. Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in subtlety, yet not described by subtlety; عظِيم in greatness, yet not described by greatness; Great in majesty, yet not described by magnitude; Majestic in exaltedness, yet not described by coarseness."

He is before everything, yet it is not said that anything is before Him; and after everything, yet it is not said that there is an after for Him. He willed things not through resolve; He is all-aware not through device; He is in all things without being mixed with them, and not separate from them. He is Manifest, not in the sense of direct contact; self-disclosing, not through the commencement of vision; far, not by distance; near, not by closeness; subtle, not by corporeality; existent, not after nonexistence.

He is an Agent, not by compulsion; an Ordainer, not by movement; a Willer, not by inclination; Hearing, not by an instrument; Seeing, not by a tool. Places do not contain Him, times do not encompass Him, attributes do not limit Him, and slumbers do not overtake Him. His being precedes times, His existence precedes nonexistence, and His pre-eternity precedes beginning.

By His endowing the faculties with perception, it is known that He has no faculty; by His bringing forth substances, it is known that He has no substance; by His placing opposites among things, it is known that He has no opposite; and by His pairing things together, it is known that He has no companion. He set light against darkness, dryness against moisture, roughness against softness, and cold against heat.

He joins together its mutually hostile things and separates its closely related things; by their separation they indicate the One who separated them, and by their composition they indicate the One who composed them.
And that is His, the Exalted, saying: "And of every thing We created pairs, that perhaps you may take heed."
So He separated between before and after, so that it may be known that there is no before for Him and no after for Him.

Their innate dispositions testify that there is no disposition for the One who instilled them; their temporality informs that there is no time for the One who assigned them time. He veiled some of them from others so that it may be known that there is no veil between Him and His creation. He was Lord when there was no one lorded over, God when there was none worshipped, Knowing when there was nothing known, and Hearing when there was nothing heard.

key_terms.الْأَوْقَاتُ: times, which do not encompass or delimit Allah
key_terms.بِحَقَائِقِ الْإِيمَانِ: through the true realities of faith by which the hearts know Allah
key_terms.قَرِينَ: a counterpart or associate, which Allah does not have
key_terms.لَطِيفُ اللَّطَافَةِ: utterly subtle beyond created notions of subtlety

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (عليه السلام) describe seeing Allah and His divine attributes?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a profound exposition of tawhid from Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام), affirming that Allah is not perceived by physical sight but known by the hearts through the realities of iman. It negates corporeality, limitation, temporality, and likeness from Allah while showing that the created order, with its opposites and pairings, points to the absolute transcendence and uniqueness of its Creator.
